newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Celtech makes firm debut on SAfrica bourse.
newsitem.headline: Celtech makes firm debut on SAfrica bourse.

text.p: Celtron Technologies on Wednesday made a firm debut in brisk trade on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) with dealers saying the company had a good earnings potential.
"The listing went exceptionally well. It has been taken positively by the market. It looks like it has more growth potential and the share could still rise," one dealer said.

The share opened at 400 cents and touched a high of 470 cents before settling at 440 shares at 1000 GMT. It was the most actively traded share on the exchange with over 2.6 million shares changing hands valued at over 11.5 million rand.

The company forecast earnings for the year to end September at 13.46 cents a share rising to 70.83 cents in 1998. It said it expected to declare a dividend of 4.04 cents this year which was seen jumping to 21.25 cents next year.
The main reason for listing was to raise capital to finance a number of big contracts, the company said.
